sections.title: Types of Numbers
sections.content: Number System begins with understanding different types of numbers. Natural numbers are counting numbers (1, 2, 3...). Whole numbers include 0. Integers include negative numbers. Rational numbers can be written in the form p/q where q is not zero. Irrational numbers cannot be written in fractional form and have non-terminating, non-repeating decimals.

sections.title: Even and Odd Numbers
sections.content: A number divisible by 2 is even. A number not divisible by 2 is odd. Even + Even = Even. Odd + Odd = Even. Even + Odd = Odd. Even × Even = Even. Odd × Odd = Odd. These basic properties are frequently used in simple reasoning questions.

sections.title: Basic Divisibility Rules
sections.content: Divisibility by 2: Last digit is even. By 3: Sum of digits divisible by 3. By 4: Last two digits divisible by 4. By 5: Last digit is 0 or 5. By 8: Last three digits divisible by 8. By 9: Sum of digits divisible by 9. By 10: Last digit is 0.

sections.title: Factors and Multiples
sections.content: A factor divides a number exactly. A multiple is obtained by multiplying a number with integers. To find factors, check divisibility up to the square root of the number. Prime numbers have exactly two factors: 1 and the number itself.

sections.title: HCF and LCM Basics
sections.content: HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the greatest number that divides given numbers exactly. LCM (Least Common Multiple) is the smallest number divisible by given numbers. For two numbers: HCF × LCM = Product of the numbers.

sections.title: Decimals and Fractions
sections.content: Fractions represent parts of a whole. A terminating decimal has limited digits after decimal point. A non-terminating repeating decimal can be converted into fraction using algebraic method. A fraction in simplest form has no common factor between numerator and denominator.

sections.title: Square and Cube Numbers
sections.content: A perfect square is obtained by multiplying a number by itself. A perfect cube is obtained by multiplying a number three times. Numbers ending in 2, 3, 7, or 8 cannot be perfect squares. Recognizing these patterns helps in quick elimination.

tricks.title: Quick Even-Odd Check
tricks.explanation: Look only at the last digit to determine whether a number is even or odd.
tricks.example: 746 ends with 6, so it is even.

tricks.title: Digit Sum Trick for 3 and 9
tricks.explanation: Add the digits repeatedly until a single digit is obtained.

tricks.title: Fast HCF Idea
tricks.explanation: If one number divides another completely, the smaller number is the HCF.

tricks.title: LCM Shortcut for Co-Prime Numbers
tricks.explanation: If two numbers are co-prime, their LCM is simply their product.

tricks.title: Perfect Square Elimination
tricks.explanation: Check the last digit before attempting full calculation.
tricks.example: 123 cannot be a perfect square because it ends in 3.

tricks.title: Factor Pair Method
tricks.explanation: Check divisibility only up to square root and write factor pairs together.

tricks.title: Terminating Decimal Check
tricks.explanation: If denominator has only 2 and 5 as prime factors, decimal will terminate.

tricks.title: Square Root Approximation
tricks.explanation: Locate nearest perfect squares to estimate quickly.
tricks.example: √50 lies between √49 and √64, so it is slightly more than 7.
